transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-04 15:00 PT — Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dmitri (QuantumVeil CTO), Sara (Infra Lead), Aisha (Security), Tomás (Network)
Summary: Short discovery focused on private/VPC deployment readiness. Customer wants strict data residency, egress control, and can consider Dedicated or Private control plane. Key risks: region lock for EU-only data, existing NAT/proxy path, internal compliance review timeline.
Topics: private endpoints, VPC peering vs transit gateway, egress IPs, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 audit artifacts, staging-to-prod onramp, latency expectations.
Auto-generated action items: (see metadata)
Questions: how does Redwood handle private egress, what are peering topology options, can we key-manage models with customer KMS, what are typical pilot timelines?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya with Redwood Inference. we'll run through networking readiness and what a private onramp looks like. quick intros?
[00:08] Dmitri: yeah hi i'm dmitri, cto at quantumveil. we run a mix of gcp and on-prem, we have strict eu data residency, and security's main blocker until network's sorted.
[00:17] Sara: Sara here, infra lead. we own vpc layout, transit, nat, and the k8s clusters.
[00:22] Aisha: Aisha, security, i care about KMS, audit logs, and segmentation.
[00:26] Liam: Liam from Redwood infra / se side. i'll be the technical owner for the connectivity side.
[00:31] Tomás: Tomás, network, i'll send the current egress config after.
[00:35] Maya: great, high level—two options you're looking at: Redwood Hosted (fast) vs Dedicated/Private (our reserved pools + VPC private control plane). since security's here i'm guessing private is on the table?
[00:45] Dmitri: correct. for production we need the control plane in our VPC or at least private endpoints. we cannot send PII out to public endpoints.
[00:52] Maya: understood. to check our assumptions — is the requirement that all inference traffic stays inside eu-west-1, or are there a few services that can be in us?
[00:59] Sara: must stay eu-west-1 for model inference; metadata logs can be in us but we prefer everything in eu.
[01:06] Aisha: also want customer-managed KMS for model encryption and HSM-backed keys for highest tier data.
[01:12] Liam: ok makes sense. two common topologies: 1) Private endpoints (privatelink style) + VPC peering to Redwood-managed subnets, or 2) Transit gateway with peering to our dedicated pool in the customer's VPC. each has tradeoffs.
[01:28] Tomás: we're leaning toward transit gateway because we can centralize routing and egress via our existing proxy. but worried about IP overlap and route tables.
[01:36] Liam: right, overlap's a pain. we usually ask for a /20 or larger for the Redwood-hosted subnet in peering model to avoid collisions, or we can do NAT-ing on a dedicated edge. for transit gateway we can do explicit route filters and we support BGP route exchange in some regions.
[01:51] Dmitri: how do you handle egress? our compliance needs a set of stable egress IPs for allowlisting — we also have an outbound proxy that all traffic must pass through.
[01:59] Liam: we can publish a fixed egress IP set for the dedicated pool in the region; for private deployments we can also terminate inside your VPC so egress is under your control. if you keep on-prem proxy in the path we'll route through it.
[02:11] Sara: ok do you support PrivateLink / privatelink equivalents on GCP? most of our infra is gcp.
[02:18] Liam: GCP uses Private Service Connect for privatelink-like behaviour. Redwood supports PSC, AWS Privatelink, and Azure Private Link. we have a couple of customers on each. some transcription note: we had earlier customers call it 'privatelink' generically.
[02:32] Aisha: on the compliance side we need TLS termination? where are certs managed? we want mTLS and mutual auth from our side.
[02:39] Liam: we support mTLS and customer-supplied certs for private endpoints. keys can be managed in your KMS — we support wrapping model artifacts and in-flight encryption; stitching with your HSM is possible but needs engineering time.
[02:51] Maya: timeline question — what's realistic for a pilot once we have network details?
[02:56] Liam: usually 2-3 weeks to stand up a test VPC peering or private endpoint, then 48 hours of benchmark runs. if there's KMS/HSM integration, add 2 weeks for security review and integration testing.
[03:08] Dmitri: cost tradeoffs — Dedicated reserved GPU pools vs Redwood Hosted — our main metric is token latency under 200ms for small prompt, and predictable throughput for peak hours.
[03:19] Maya: Dedicated gives you isolation and predictable latency; Hosted is cheaper to start. we can run a small Dedicated pilot with a commit for the month to ensure SLOs. also Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization to reduce token cost.
[03:31] Sara: what about KV cache and batching? we have chat workloads with long context, we'd like shared KV cache to reduce cost.
[03:38] Liam: runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching. in Dedicated mode you can pin model instances with warmed KV cache; Private deployments allow cache persistence to reduce token generation. downside: cache persistence uses more memory per shard.
[03:50] Tomás: network nitty gritty — do you require any specific ports or NAT traversal? we run strict egress 443 only plus our agent outbound.
[03:57] Liam: we only need HTTPS (443) for control plane ops unless you opt for a data-plane peering where we put subnets into your VPC. in that case we need TCP/UDP for some internal telemetry but we can tunnel over 443 if necessary.
[04:12] Aisha: audit logs — can we ship full request logs to our SIEM? retention and redaction?
[04:18] Maya: yes, logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint — we mask PII by default if you choose. for Private deployment you get raw access to audit logs and longer retention as an add-on.
[04:28] Dmitri: are there any region gating issues — e.g., certain newer model variants only in us-east? we need to make sure eu models are available or we accept latency hit for cross-region calls.
[04:37] Liam: model availability varies; some experimental variants may be cloud-region limited. our recommended approach: pin to a eu-verified model for prod; we can also host a quantized EU variant in your Dedicated pool. if you see cross-region fallback it'll be logged and we can block it with routing policy.
[04:52] Sara: ok. who signs the network diagram? we need a formal topo to pass our internal architecture review.
[04:58] Maya: we'll provide a network checklist and a draft diagram. Liam will produce the peering/ transit / privatelink options with CIDR suggestions.
[05:06] Liam: also note NAT gateways and proxy: we'll need the egress ip list if you want to lock traffic to your allowlist. and we recommend a non-overlapping CIDR block — if you can't allocate one we can use NAT with a dedicated edge.
[05:19] Tomás: we may have overlapping /16s across teams, that's why transit gateway appealed to us.
[05:24] Liam: transit helps centralize but requires careful route table management; we can provide example terraform snippets for the peering and route policies.
[05:32] Aisha: security controls: RBAC, SSO/SAML integration for the console, audit trails — are those available in Private?
[05:39] Maya: yes RBAC and SSO are available across Dedicated and Private. private control plane gives you fine-grained org policies and audit export.
[05:46] Dmitri: excellent. one more question — we are curious about pen test scheduling and whether Redwood will be in scope for our annual audit.
[05:52] Maya: we provide SOC2 artifacts and can coordinate pen tests with our security team. for Private deployments we do a joint review and provide expected window for tests.
[05:59] Dmitri: sounds good, i'll need a package of docs for our security review.
[06:03] Maya: noted — we'll push SOC2, network checklist, and sample topo links. also a Request: please share your egress IPs and any proxy ACLs.
[06:12] Tomás: i'll share after the call.
[06:15] Sara: timeline wise, we're aiming for a security signoff by end of november. can you align with that?
[06:21] Liam: yes if we get the network details this week we can turn around the draft topo by 11/10 and have a pilot in mid nov.
[06:29] Closing recap (rough):
- Customer requirement: EU-only inference in eu-west-1, customer KMS/HSM, allowlisted egress IPs, mTLS to private endpoints.
- Calls of action: Redwood to share Private deployment checklist, CIDR recommendations, sample Terraform, SOC2 + security docs.
- Customer to share egress IPs, proxy/NAT notes, and compliance timeline.

Crosstalk and small clarifications observed, some ASR errors in proper nouns (e.g., 'privatelink' vs PSC), timestamps approximated.
